summary: ASTRIA-NAVIGATOR 3D is a hybrid landing-security framework designed for lunar South Pole missions. It resolves the critical resolution gap of LOLA orbital data (5–20m) by deploying a coordinated swarm of 4 micro-scout vehicles (⁠Scout-Alpha N1-N4⁠) using Voronoi spatial optimization to achieve 2 cm/pixel centimeter-level 3D topography. Powered by solid-state LLZO batteries and automated AI safety brakes, the system prevents lander tipping, overcomes mountain shadows, and ensures safe, autonomous lunar exploration.
details:
Function & How It Works: A hybrid navigation system combining a 4-scout lunar rover swarm and a 3D web control dashboard. It uses 1550nm LiDAR scanning to map terrain at ultra-high resolution (2 cm/pixel) and detects hazards in real-time.

Tools & Technologies: Open3D/PCL for point cloud processing, Python for AI edge-computing algorithms, 3D web visualization tools, and hardware simulations for solid-state power systems (TEG/Micro-RTG).

Creative Aspect: Decentralized local processing on rovers, dynamic Z-Axis mast deployment to escape mountain shadows, and automated AI emergency braking (18ms response).

Expected Impact: Completely eliminates lander tipping hazards, ensures structural safety, and guarantees continuous 24/7 operational capability in extreme polar environments.
